# A DIY Watch You Can Actually Wear

In the ever-evolving landscape of wearable technology, a new contender has emerged that promises to meet the desires of both enthusiasts and practical users alike: the T-Watch Ultra by LILYGO. This smartwatch, engineered specifically for the ESP32 hacking community, boasts an impressive array of features combined with rugged durability, making it a standout option for those seeking a DIY experience that doesn’t compromise on functionality.

## Rugged Durability Meets Advanced Features

The T-Watch Ultra is designed with an IP65-rated case, ensuring protection against rain, spills, and dust—common enemies of traditional smartwatches. Inside this robust exterior lies the powerful ESP32-S3 microcontroller, equipped with a dual-core Tensilica LX7 CPU that operates at speeds of up to 240 MHz. Coupled with 16MB of flash memory and 8MB of PSRAM, this smartwatch is not only capable of handling everyday tasks but is also well-suited for complex applications, including edge AI tasks that can elevate its functionality.

One of the notable features is its vibrant 2.01-inch AMOLED display, with a resolution of 410×502 and capacitive touch support, allowing for a user-friendly interface. Additionally, the T-Watch Ultra is powered by a 1,100mAh battery, which enhances usability and runtime, ensuring that users can rely on it throughout the day without frequent recharges.

Connectivity is another strong suit of the T-Watch Ultra. It supports Wi-Fi, Bluetooth 5.0 LE, and even features a Semtech SX1262 LoRa transceiver, providing a range of communication options. For those interested in location tracking, the built-in GNSS module offers accurate positioning, while the Bosch BHI260AP smart sensor introduces motion-based AI capabilities.

## A Community-Driven Development Platform

What sets the T-Watch Ultra apart is its commitment to the DIY ethos. It is compatible with Arduino, MicroPython, and ESP-IDF, making it accessible for developers and hobbyists alike. An ecosystem of example code and libraries is available to assist users in exploring the vast potential of this smartwatch. Pre-orders are currently being accepted at a reasonable price of $78.32, which positions it as a practical alternative to existing DIY smartwatches that often fall short in terms of durability.

## Conversations from the Community

The announcement of the T-Watch Ultra has sparked lively discussions among tech enthusiasts on platforms like Hacker News. While some users appreciate the watch's capabilities, others debate the definition of "DIY" in the context of modern smartwatches. One commenter expressed disappointment over the lack of true DIY options, stating that they build their devices from scratch, including the PCB and 3D-printed cases.
